title: Studies on the role of interdisciplinary boards in clinical genetic care
summary: A tumor predisposition is a genetic condition that increases a person's likelihood of developing certain types of cancer. The clinical care of individuals with suspected or confirmed tumor predispositions is often complex and typically requires the involvement of multiple medical specialties. The GenBoard study investigates the significance of interdisciplinary case conferences (boards) in clinical care. The aim of the study is to improve the care of individuals with confirmed or suspected tumor predispositions.
conditions: Neoplasms of uncertain or unknown behaviour

interventions.name: Individuals with a diagnosis or suspected diagnosis of tumor predisposition. Collection of the initial status from the documentation of the board, supplemented if necessary by data from the HIS or other patient data (e.g., external medical reports). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis or suspected diagnosis of a tumor predisposition syndrome
- Inpatient treatment or outpatient presentation at the University Hospital Augsburg or one of the partner institutions
- Written consent of the patient or the legal representative to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients or their legal representatives without sufficient German language skills
